name: The Weft Arrangement
motto: The gap between what is owed and what is paid is where we live.
description:
The Weft Arrangement began not as an organization but as an accounting practice. In the wake of PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION's 2177 mass contract termination of its Laceworks residential maintenance workforce — a decision that left approximately 1,400 workers without severance, housing guarantees, or neural augmentation upkeep coverage — a group of former site supervisors began keeping a shared ledger of what Palladian owed the people it had discarded. They called it the Weft, after the horizontal threads in a weave, because they were tracking what ran across and beneath the visible structure. The ledger was initially just a record of grievance, a way of making the loss legible. It became something more when one of the original keepers, a structural materials specialist named Cours Aldine, realized the ledger could be used to coordinate: if you knew what everyone was owed and what everyone had, you could route resources, skills, and labor to fill the gaps without money changing hands at all.

The Weft Arrangement now functions as a sophisticated labor and resource exchange network operating primarily across the Laceworks and the lower Circuit, with significant nodes in Old Harbor and Substation Null. Its core operation is the Ledger, a continuously updated encrypted record of skills offered, needs declared, and exchanges completed among its roughly 3,000 active participants. The Weft does not use currency internally. Every transaction is denominated in what members call thread — a non-transferable unit of account that tracks contribution and need without creating accumulation. A retired OUROBOROS ENERGY grid technician maintains electrical systems for a block of Laceworks residential units; a former IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS hydroponics operator grows supplemental food in a repurposed sublevel corridor; a ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC washout with relevant training handles basic augmentation troubleshooting. The exchange happens through the Ledger, and the Ledger is maintained by a rotating body of Keepers who also serve as dispute mediators.

What makes the Weft Arrangement genuinely distinctive in the GLMZ ecosystem is its relationship to corporate infrastructure. The network was built almost entirely by people who spent careers inside major corponations and left — voluntarily or otherwise — with deep technical knowledge of those systems. Weft members can maintain OUROBOROS grid taps because they know exactly how OUROBOROS meters its sublevel feeds. They can grow food in repurposed PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION infrastructure because they know which substrates were spec'd for load and which were cut. This is not sabotage and the Weft is careful to frame it otherwise — they call it maintenance, and in a technical sense they are correct, because without the Weft's informal labor, significant portions of the Laceworks' residential infrastructure would have degraded beyond habitability years ago. The corponations know this. PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION in particular has reached a studied non-acknowledgment of the Weft's existence that functions as a form of tacit permission, because the alternative is owning the maintenance liability they abandoned.
ideology: The Weft Arrangement is ideologically skeptical of ideology. Its founding documents — a set of operating principles Cours Aldine drafted and the original Keepers ratified — explicitly reject both revolutionary framing and charitable framing in favor of what they call accurate accounting. Their position is that the corponation tier has externalized enormous costs onto its former workforce and onto Laceworks residents generally, and that the Weft is simply a mechanism for those costs to be met by the people who actually understand them, outside the pricing structures that would make meeting them impossible. They are not trying to replace the system; they are trying to survive its accounting errors. This pragmatism is both a genuine philosophical position and a practical shield — it makes the Weft much harder to frame as a threat than a more explicitly political organization would be.
territory: Core operations in the Laceworks (particularly the residential mid-levels and sublevel corridors), lower Circuit undermarket, Old Harbor dock worker residential blocks, and Substation Null peripheral zones. The Ledger is accessible anywhere with a compatible encrypted mesh connection, and the Weft has passive participants across a much wider area.
leadership: The Weft Arrangement is governed by a body of seven active Keepers elected by participant vote on two-year staggered terms, with a Ledger Arbiter — currently Cours Aldine, re-elected four consecutive times and increasingly regarded as irreplaceable in ways that make some members uncomfortable — who serves as final mediator for contested exchanges and the public face of the network when one is required. Other notable figures include Ysel Tamm, a former ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC systems auditor who now manages the Ledger's technical infrastructure and is widely believed to be the only person who fully understands its architecture; and Roan Pressfield, an Old Harbor node coordinator and former ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logistics contractor who handles the network's most sensitive resource acquisitions.
methods: Maintaining the encrypted Ledger as a real-time exchange platform for skills, labor, and material resources denominated in non-transferable thread units
Rotating Keeper mediation for exchange disputes and community governance
Grid tap maintenance and power redistribution using detailed institutional knowledge of OUROBOROS ENERGY sublevel infrastructure
Unauthorized but technically legitimate use of abandoned PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION infrastructure for food production, fabrication, and housing
Skill-matching for members navigating corporate bureaucracies including TESSERA citizenship appeals and LAZARUS pharmaceutical licensing exceptions
Informal apprenticeship and technical knowledge transfer to reduce participant dependency on corporate service providers
Strategic non-documentation of certain exchanges to maintain the Weft's framing as informal community maintenance rather than organized economic activity
Quiet leverage of corporate non-acknowledgment as protection against enforcement
resources: The Ledger: a sophisticated encrypted exchange platform representing years of participant contribution data
Deep institutional technical knowledge of OUROBOROS ENERGY, PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION, ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC, IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS, and ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS infrastructure and systems
Repurposed PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION sublevel infrastructure across the Laceworks
Functioning informal power and water distribution networks maintained outside corporate metering
3,000+ active participants representing a wide range of skilled trades and technical specializations
PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION's tacit non-interference, which functions as a form of institutional cover
Encrypted mesh network infrastructure for Ledger access and internal communication

relationships.description: The Tessera Residuals' population of former TESSERA CORPONATION workers overlaps significantly with the Weft's participant base. Many Residuals members use the Ledger for resource exchange, and the Weft has provided technical support for several Residuals community infrastructure projects. Neither organization formally acknowledges the relationship, which suits both.

Palladian Negative's infrastructure disruption activities directly threaten the PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION sublevel systems the Weft depends on and has spent years maintaining. The Weft views Palladian Negative as reckless actors who will destroy the conditions that make survival possible in the Laceworks. Palladian Negative views the Weft as collaborators who have made peace with the infrastructure of their own exploitation. The tension occasionally turns into active interference.

The Sutured Commons and the Weft Arrangement operate in overlapping territory with compatible philosophies and non-competing functions. Weft members have provided Stitch House infrastructure maintenance; Sutured Commons members have provided care to Weft participants outside the Ledger system as a gesture of solidarity. No formal relationship exists, but there is mutual awareness and goodwill.

The Seam Registry's interest in tracking undocumented population movements in the Laceworks creates friction with the Weft's deliberate non-documentation practices. The Weft suspects the Registry has attempted to cross-reference Ledger participation patterns with Registry data. The Registry views the Weft's opacity as an obstacle to what it considers legitimate cartographic work.

The Franchise Compact's microeconomy operations in the Laceworks undermarket occasionally compete with Weft exchange networks for the same participants and resources. The Compact has made several overtures suggesting formalized integration; the Weft has declined each time on the grounds that the Compact's currency-based model is structurally incompatible with thread accounting. The Compact finds this answer unsatisfying.

story_hooks: Ysel Tamm has gone silent. She missed two consecutive Keeper meetings, her mesh node has gone cold, and no one in the Ledger network has logged a transaction with her in nine days. The Ledger's technical infrastructure is still running, but Cours Aldine has discovered that someone has been making small, difficult-to-detect modifications to the exchange architecture — either Tamm before she disappeared, or someone since.

PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION has quietly hired a new infrastructure assessment team to conduct a sublevel survey of the Laceworks. The Weft's tacit arrangement with Palladian depends on Palladian not officially knowing what the Weft has done with its abandoned infrastructure. An official survey would end that arrangement. Roan Pressfield needs to know who authorized the survey and whether it can be redirected, delayed, or made to reach the right conclusions.

A new participant has joined the Weft Arrangement with an extraordinary skill set — deep knowledge of TESSERA CORPONATION's citizenship tier data architecture that would be enormously useful to the network. Their Ledger contributions have been generous and technically impeccable. Cours Aldine has a persistent feeling something is wrong and cannot articulate why.

A Ledger dispute has escalated beyond normal Keeper mediation. A long-standing participant claims another participant failed to deliver on a thread commitment involving medical equipment that a third party's life depended on. The accused claims the commitment was never formally logged. The Ledger shows no record, but two witnesses say the exchange was agreed verbally. The outcome of the mediation will set a precedent the entire network is watching.

OUROBOROS ENERGY has begun a sublevel grid audit in the Laceworks using new detection hardware that can identify the specific tap configurations the Weft uses. The audit is framed as routine maintenance. It is not. The Weft has two weeks before the audit reaches its primary power nodes.

Cours Aldine has received a private approach from a VANTABLACK MEDIA journalist working on a long-form documentary about informal economies in the Laceworks. The journalist claims to be sympathetic and has offered to anonymize all sources. Aldine knows that any public attention on the Weft — positive or negative — could dissolve the studied non-acknowledgment that PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION has maintained for years. The journalist, however, knows things about the Weft that they should not know, which raises the question of who has already been talking.
